title: Harlow Foods v. Pennine Logistics
note: Liability cap upheld between commercial parties of equal bargaining power; the cap applied even to deliberate breach because the wording covered any breach.

title: Greyfield Software v. Marlowe Bank
note: An uncapped indemnity for any and all losses was read narrowly to third party claims only, because the contract elsewhere capped direct losses.

title: Otter Cloud v. Bramble Retail
note: Termination for convenience without notice was valid, but the customer still owed payment for work done before termination under an implied term.

title: Kestrel Design v. Juniper Homes
note: A clause assigning all IP created during the term did not capture the designer's pre-existing templates; background IP needs express words.

title: Northgate Media v. Ash Analytics
note: A five year worldwide non-compete on a supplier was struck down as an unreasonable restraint of trade; a twelve month non-solicit survived.

title: Lumen Health v. Calder Systems
note: A warranty that software is error free was breached by minor defects; damages were limited by the liability cap.

title: Briar Energy v. Fenwick Engineering
note: A pandemic did not excuse late payment because the force majeure clause covered performance, not payment obligations.

title: Quayside Hotels v. Rowan Linen
note: An auto renewal with a 180 day notice window was enforced; the court noted the clause was clear and the customer was a sophisticated party.

title: Hollis Pharma v. Stark Labs
note: Trade secrets stayed protected after a one year confidentiality term expired, under the general law of confidence.

title: Mere Transport v. Clyde Ports
note: A floating governing law clause letting one party choose the law later was held void for uncertainty; the court applied the law of closest connection.

title: Tamar Retail v. Vale Payments
note: Ninety day payment terms in a small supplier contract were challenged under late payment rules; statutory interest applied after sixty days.

title: Sable Telecom v. Orchard Data
note: An audit at any time without notice was limited to reasonable times and frequency by an implied duty of good faith.
